subject: Australian memorandum / Bahnson CIA-cutout allegation
status: documented archival paper + documented physics history; claimed intelligence link not corroborated
scope: The signed Australian JIO memorandum (NAA A13693/3092/2/000, May 1971) is genuine. Kaiser and Rickles document Bahnson financing real general-relativity research, the Wheeler/UNC firewall, and independent 1958 electrostatic evaluations. These do not corroborate the separate alleged CIA cutout operation.
stronger_evidence: 2018 archival study with citations to Wheeler memo 28 Nov 1955 (BDW), Palmatier 13 Aug 1958 (CDWM), and the original 1971 Australian document.
limitation: No contemporaneous primary CIA/Australian file has been located naming Bahnson as an intermediary in the specific arrangement alleged by the interview. Do not infer CIA relationship from a published paper about university physics.
closure_requirement: Item-level CIA/OSS/AFOSI or Australian archival file explicitly connecting the named Bahnson with the specific operation and dates, plus exact interview audio passage resolving antecedents.

subject: Medieval edict / Magonia sky-ship narrative
status: original weather-magic decree and separate medieval critical account identified; aerial reporting law absent
scope: Admonitio generalis (789) c.65 prohibits tempestarii, spells and augury. Agobard De grandine et tonitruis, surviving BnF Latin 2853, describes and disputes Magonia cloud-ship accusations; it is not a reporting mandate.
stronger_evidence: Ninth-century manuscript and scholarly critical Latin editions already cited in Edition 8, together with separate early-modern Comte de Gabalis annotation genealogy.
limitation: No independently attested Carolingian law demanding reports about alien visitors has been located; absence from these identified texts does not demonstrate impossibility of an unrelated lost manuscript.
closure_requirement: Produce a dateable medieval manuscript witness or critical-edition citation with the exact alleged reporting-language, distinct from both texts.

subject: Puharich entire Tesla / TMT manuscript
status: contemporaneous self-citation + family publishing account + first-person copy-holder corroborated as records; full manuscript not accessed
scope: Puharich cites TMT, The Magnetic Threat in his 1984 paper as unpublished under contract with Dell. A family memoir describes a 1978 submission to editor Christopher Kuppig, but does not prove the alleged interference. Tesla historian Marc Seifer (2022) says he possesses a copy and describes a longer manuscript title and topics. RT17 advertises a 49.53-MB scan.
stronger_evidence: Dated 1984 authorial bibliography, memoir publishing narrative and named living copy-holder; exact online scan endpoint https://www.rt17.hr/download/11490/.
limitation: The RT17 binary download could not be retrieved in this environment; Seifer copy, publisher contract, and a title-page comparison remain uninspected. Manuscript arguments are not established physical facts.
closure_requirement: Obtain complete PDF or physical copy from RT17 or the identified holder; log SHA256, page count, title page and publication provenance; compare with cited anthology and the 1984 self-citation.

subject: 1947 Twining / Schulgen variants and Horten evidence
status: 1947 originals and two later published textual variants identified; interview-held copy still unknown
scope: Twining Sep 23 is separate from the late-Oct Schulgen collection request. December 16 Berlin Command report interviews multiple technical persons and records denials of saucer-like designs. McCoy correspondence cites RAE AERO 1703 and unverified aircraft intelligence. A 1997 Philip Klass article reports Robert Todd’s original-vs-1986-published version comparison, with altered Russian-vs-interplanetary wording.
stronger_evidence: 1947 Project 1947 transcribed military reports, a NARA-correspondence-backed original Schulgen facsimile, and contemporaneous 1997 printed commentary reproducing paragraph contrast.
limitation: Original scan of the exact printout shown by the interview speaker not available. Klass/Todd published an alteration allegation; not independently proven who altered the text. Also USSR production report is an intelligence lead, not verified delivery.
closure_requirement: Get photograph or scan of the speaker’s exact document with pagination; compare line-by-line to 1947 facsimile and 1986 variant, including headers, transmittal, typefaces and annotations.

subject: Vatican / Mussolini Magenta transfer papers
status: claimant provenance, internal date contradiction and Vatican institutional position documented; dossier unauthenticated
scope: Roberto Pinotti describes anonymous batches received from 1996 and gives conflicting incident dates (April 11 and June 13 1933) within one text. The 2024 Catholic News Service interviews Vatican archive official Marco Grilli, who says relevant extraterrestrial documents are not held in Vatican Apostolic Archive.
stronger_evidence: Pinotti’s own reproduced first-person narrative and separately quoted official statement, along with known anonymous custody break and a reportedly lost 30-page packet.
limitation: Neither an accessioned Vatican holding nor independent 1933 contemporary reporting of a recovered non-human craft was located. The Vatican official statement cannot adjudicate hypothetical undiscovered material, while Pinotti’s claim cannot authenticate itself.
closure_requirement: Original 1933 item with chain of custody and forensic record; item-level Italian / Vatican / US archives shelfmark and independent date reconciliation (April 11 vs June 13).

subject: William Stephenson to Josephine Brown telegram
status: Stephenson intelligence role and later distinct archival records verified; alleged telegram not identified
scope: CIA public history verifies Stephenson headed wartime British Security Coordination. Canada Declassified gives R219/RG25 Box 13 dossier 3-12-3 Part 1 for different 1955–56 Stephenson report correspondence. Neither matches the alleged wartime telegram to Josephine Brown. Beware other archivally documented people called William Stephenson.
stronger_evidence: CIA official institutional historical biography and exact Canadian accession of a distinct BSC document; the alleged telegram persists in later family/interview recollections only.
limitation: No dated original Stephenson–Josephine message, contemporaneous transmitted-text copy, envelope, or accession matching sender-recipient-date. A documented 1942 Navy separation telegram to another recipient is a different item.
closure_requirement: Retrieve actual telegram scan or contemporaneous incoming/outgoing message log naming sender, recipient and date and corroborate the proposed 1944/45 mission separately.
